title: 本草綱目拾遺(一)
shelf_note: Zhao Xuemin's Qing materia medica supplement, a printed Chinese text, in the general 'universallibrary' collection; the page (medicinal waters, lotus-leaf dew) matches the title.
structure_note: The structure counts give pages_translated 0, but the book's pages_translated field says 99 and this page carries a translation, so the counter and the field disagree (E2). with_printed_number is 1 of 99, which fits a Chinese print whose folio sits on the block-heart, out of frame here. No backsteps and no repeats.

ocr_errors.image: printed type in a ruled frame
ocr_errors.problem: script tag wrong: the leaf is printed, not handwritten (self-reported tag)

tr_errors.english: To treat eating a hundred urines
tr_errors.problem: a literal rendering that makes no sense; the note admits the heading is uncertain, so it does not mislead, but the reader gets nonsense. The glyph on the image is a little unclear (尿 or a 脈-like variant)

tr_errors.english: mixed with a little holy water, and taken by mouth
tr_errors.problem: 開 (dissolve or mix in) is folded into 'taken'. Acceptable, but loose

pages.layout: half-leaf of a Chinese print: ten ruled vertical columns inside a heavy frame; the entry title 荷葉上露 stands in its own column; a strip of the block-heart shows at the right edge

book_verdict: The transcription is faithful character by character, and the translation is faithful with sensible glosses. The only problems are an odd literal heading, which the translation flags itself, a wrong 'handwritten' script tag, and a book-level counter that disagrees with the page-count field.
